title: Every authored docs/ .adoc declares a non-empty :doc-id: and :status:

facts.note: Every authored AsciiDoc file beneath docs/, whether new, edited or untouched; docs/dist/** is excluded.
Produced by the docs_capability validator header scan over all files in scope.

fires: Planner authors a new .adoc under docs/ (e.g. docs/architecture/, docs/purpose/, docs/archive/).
Any existing docs/ .adoc, changed or not, lacks :doc-id: or :status:, or one of them has an empty value.
A docs/ .adoc has no AsciiDoc header at all.

given: An authored .adoc under docs/ (not docs/dist/), new or existing
when: docs are planned, written or validated
then: Its header declares non-empty :doc-id: and :status: attributes.
prefer: Declare both in the header above the first section: `= Shared Control Root` / `:doc-id: architecture.shared-control-root` / `:status: current`.
Prefix doc-id with its area (`architecture.`, `purpose.`, `archive.`) so id and tree agree; readability only, unchecked.
avoid: Declaring only one: id without status has unknown currency; status without id is a claim nothing can reference.
Using a path as identity; doc-id is the only graph node id.
Skipping header-less files; they are violations.

Treating status as making archive/ honest: it cannot say superseded by what; the supersedes edge does (validated by planner.docs.graph-target-resolves). This rule only provides identity; it does not alone discharge the archival-currency issue.
why: Edges resolve only against declared doc-ids, so an undeclared document can be neither referenced nor found missing; status makes current-versus-historical readable.
evidence: docs_capability validator reports no identity finding for any .adoc under docs/ outside docs/dist/.
Reviewer sees non-empty :doc-id: and :status: in the header of each docs/ .adoc.
verifier_detail: Scan every .adoc beneath docs/, excluding docs/dist/**, regardless of whether it changed.
Finding when :doc-id: is absent or empty; finding when :status: is absent or empty.
A file with no AsciiDoc header at all is a violation, not a skip; silence about a document that declares nothing is the failure mode this extension exists to refuse.
Term `doc_id`: the value of the :doc-id: attribute, a dotted identifier such as architecture.shared-control-root; the ONLY node identity the documentation graph uses; paths are never node identities.
Term `status`: the value of the :status: attribute, one of current, superseded, historical; answers 'is this accepted truth today?'. Source requires non-empty.
Area-prefix/tree agreement of doc-id is NOT enforced; do not report it.
Declared doc-ids form the set planner.docs.graph-target-resolves resolves every edge against; supersedes edges are validated there, not here.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.
doc-id is the node identity per spec 2 §5.1; spec 2 §5.2: status says 'this is superseded' but cannot say 'by what' — the supersedes edge carries that.
status is the flag issue #1782 exists to introduce; this rule establishes the identity the supersedes edge needs but does not by itself discharge #1782.
Content summary: identity and currency, declared in the document itself.
Severity 2, disposition strict (fails on every finding; no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline).

sharedNodes.text: strict: fails on every finding; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

additions.justification: Required by schema; derived from the source path scope and exceptions.
Schema requires a when; phrased as an invariant over all in-scope files (new or existing), not a change gate.
Schema requires evidence; restates the source obligation as a verification step.
